prerequisites: Student explains and interprets theoretical and experimental results, technical documentation, phenomena and processes in the field of mechanical engineering in general; Performing occupational safety for the laboratory: General conditions and specific conditions

learning_outcomes.text: Be aware of the fundamental concepts of Strength of Materials.
Know aspects regarding material behavior, test specimens used for material testing, classification of solid bodies, ways of supporting bodies, support conditions.
Be aware of the four types of simple stresses.
Be able to perform a simple calculation of reactions from supports.
Be aware of external loads, internal forces, classification of stresses.
Be able to determine the relationships between loads and forces, and between forces and stresses.
Know what displacements mean and what deformations represent.
Be able to establish relationships between stresses and deformations.
Be aware of the phenomenon called transverse contraction under tensile stress.

For all four simple stresses, namely tension/compression, shear, torsion, bending, the student will be able to perform the following types of calculations: figuring reactions from supports; calculating reactions according to what was learned in Theoretical Mechanics, supplemented with knowledge from Strength of Materials; dividing the bar into regions and figuring sections for each region; determining the variation of sectional forces for each region; analyzing the stress state by visualizing the variation of sectional forces; determining the most stressed area; dimensioning the cross-section in the most stressed area; performing modifications of the body's configuration in relation to optimization conditions (bodies of equal strength); calculating buckling, for bar systems, truss beams, fatigue calculation, and elements of elasticity theory.
Respect teaching staff during lectures, seminars, and laboratory sessions in interaction.
Respect disciplinary and professional indications of teaching staff for lectures, seminars, and laboratory sessions.
Form working groups for laboratory and seminar work to solve tasks provided by the teaching staff.
Document themselves before and after the course, seminar, laboratory regarding the issues that will be discussed or have been discussed on-site.
Be active in lectures, seminars, and laboratory sessions.
Take notes for laboratory work, pay attention in class, and perform calculations.
Study individually for both laboratory and seminar sessions.
Take the two tests provided in the discipline's calendar plan.

syllabus_topics: Material testing. Mechanical and elastic characteristics
Material testing, influencing factors. Simplifying hypotheses in Strength of Materials
Axial stresses, heavy bars, solid of equal strength. Axial stresses, statically indeterminate problems, resolving indeterminacy by geometric methods
Resolving indeterminacy by geometric and energy methods
Axial stresses, statically indeterminate problems, resolving indeterminacy by FEM
Bending stress, calculation of stresses and deformations
Bending, solid of equal strength, rational sections, longitudinal shear

Elements of Theory of Elasticity: General state of stress. Stress and strain tensors. Variation of stresses around a point; Principal stresses and strains, principal directions; Mohr's circles for plane and spatial state of stress.
Fundamental equations of Theory of Elasticity. Potential deformation energy (3D). Relationship between elastic characteristics (E, G and ν). Strain gauge rosette, Theories of limit state
Calculation of reactions for straight, bent, curved bars and truss beams
Axial stresses (statically determinate and indeterminate problems)
State of stress and strain. Calculation of principal stresses and strains. Drawing Mohr's circle. Stress and strain tensor
Occupational safety. Laboratory presentation. Work presentation.
Tensile test. Characteristic curve. MDSolid modeling
Demonstration of Betti's theorem. Impact bending test.
teaching_methods: Dual lecture on smart board, projecting existing course and additional clarifications using video projector
Video projector for examples of stresses, structural failures
Explanation of testing machine, devices, specimens, calculation relations, work procedures

assessment_methods.method: Systematic observation of students (part of exam)
Completion of laboratory sheets (all lab works must be done, allowing only one recovery)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must obtain a minimum grade of 5 for each of the three assessment forms: Exam, Seminar, and Laboratory. The final evaluation result is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Grades are given as integers from 1 to 10; a grade of 5 certifies the acquisition of minimum learning outcomes and the awarding of associated study credits.
